source.title: The Capability Convergence Hypothesis: Capability from Access Structure, Not Scale
source.authors: Wen-Hui Chen; Jian-Lin Chen; Zi-Yao Lin; Chi-man Vong

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present. Some mathematical symbols and formatting are garbled, but the relevant results are readable.
record.tranche_reason: Experiment A explicitly replicates PRH’s representational-convergence measurement using mutual k-NN alignment and reports how alignment varies with scale in new language-model families.
record.gate_note: Rows cover Experiment A’s own measurements of cross-family alignment and retrieval capability. The paper’s cited findings from other work and its architecture census are not rows. Experiment D measures alignment between channels within a hybrid, not between independently trained models, so it does not test these claim versions.
record.test_reason: Experiment A applies PRH's mutual k-NN alignment (k=10, max over layer pairs) to Pythia, Mamba and RWKV-4 checkpoints from 70M to 3B. These are independently trained families with different architectures. It reports how cross-family alignment changes with scale, which bears directly on V1. The rest of the paper (capability theory, census, synthetic witnesses) does not measure convergence between independently trained models.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors report that PRH's within-modality alignment-grows-with-scale pattern replicates across Pythia/Mamba/RWKV. Retrieval capability nonetheless stratifies by access structure, and alignment does not predict the capability gap (positive correlation). They frame this as observational, claiming the pattern rather than a causal attribution.
record.recipe_differences: Uses PRH’s mutual k-NN alignment approach, with k=10 and maximum alignment over layer pairs, on language-model families sharing a corpus and tokenizer; it is not a reproduction of PRH’s full range of models and settings.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors caution that taking the maximum over layer pairs favors deeper models, so absolute alignment values require care. They report that the ordering replicates across all three family pairings.

fits_no_version.finding: Despite rising cross-family alignment, retrieval capability stratifies by architecture at ~2.8B: Pythia 0.345, Mamba 0.05, RWKV 0.00. Across 74 cross-family pairs, alignment correlates positively with the absolute capability gap (+0.48; partial +0.30 controlling for scale).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Representational convergence across architectures does not imply convergence in downstream capability (e.g., in-context retrieval).

fits_no_version.finding: Experiment D: between state and index channels within one hybrid model, mutual k-NN alignment is highest at random initialization (0.576; CKA 0.993). It falls with training and with task success (solving 0.284).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Random-init components reading the same inputs show high alignment, so alignment baselines must account for input geometry; this is measured within a model, not across models.

record.problems: Experiment A is observational, uses only three language-model families trained on the same corpus and tokenizer, and does not establish causal explanations for alignment. Alignment uses maximum-over-layer-pairs, which the authors note may favor deeper models. The matched-scale retrieval margin against Mamba narrowly missed the frozen threshold at n=200 and was resolved in a follow-up at n=1000; several other scale/context cells remained below the registered margin.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows omitted. Other reported alignment results concern channels within a single hybrid, cited studies, or architectural/capability findings not measuring independently trained models’ representational convergence.

untested.parts: Different training data, objectives or modalities (corpus and tokenizer are shared). Scale beyond 3B. Non-language models.
All; no mapping, stitching or translation.
All; no feature or circuit universality.
All; k, metric and inputs are not varied. CKA is mentioned only as a check, with no reported comparison.
All; no test of plateau or completeness of alignment, and data/objective are held fixed rather than varied as a cause.

missing.what: Within-family alignment pairs, and per-pairing assignment of the three scale correlations (which pairing has 0.57, 0.87, 0.51)

record.verdict_notes: Only A1 bears on a claim version. The V7 links in the record were misapplied: those rows measure capability, not alignment completeness or its causes. Because the families share corpus and tokenizer, the V1 support covers architecture diversity only. The authors caution that max-over-layer-pairs favours deeper models, so absolute alignment values need care.

versions.untested_parts: The experiment uses three language-model families trained on the same corpus and tokenizer. It does not test different training data, objectives, or modalities, nor establish the trend at frontier scale.
No paired image-caption representations or vision-language scaling comparison.
No comparison of models trained from different seeds to assess shared features or subspaces.
No mapping, stitching, relative-representation, or unpaired interchangeability test.
No test of recurring interpretable features or circuits across models.

The primary measurement uses mutual k-NN with k=10 and max-over-layer-pairs alignment. CKA is mentioned as a check, but no comparative CKA result is given; the study does not vary similarity settings or input distributions to test metric or data dependence.

The study finds a dissociation between alignment and retrieval capability, but does not test whether alignment plateaus, whether it is incomplete in a broader sense, or whether shared data/objectives cause alignment rather than a common model of reality. Data and tokenizer are held the same, not varied.

rows.subject: Pythia, Mamba, and RWKV-4 cross-family pairings (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Measured mutual k-NN representational alignment across scale.
rows.measure: Spearman correlation between cross-family alignment and scale; alignment level relative to chance.
rows.value: Spearman 0.57/0.87/0.51 for the three pairings; n=30/24/20; all p<0.05; alignment reaches 0.7+.
rows.uncertainty: All p<0.05; no other uncertainty stated.
rows.note: The paper gives the three correlations and sample sizes in sequence but does not map each number to a specific pairing in the text; they are retained as an aggregate rather than assigned to pairs.
rows.check: Link and state are correct: alignment rises with scale for all three pairings (Spearman 0.57/0.87/0.51, all p<0.05), reaching 0.7+ against chance 0.0098. The paper does not map each correlation to a named pairing in the text. Data and tokenizer are shared across families, so only architecture varies.

rows.subject: Pythia
rows.operation_detail: Measured exact-match retrieval of templated facts at controlled context depth.
rows.uncertainty: The Pythia–Mamba margin is 32.0 ± 3.3 percentage points; the Pythia–RWKV margin is 36.5 ± 3.0 percentage points.
rows.note: The reported retrieval result shows capability differences despite rising cross-family representational alignment; the paper reports the margins separately.
rows.check: Exact-match retrieval accuracy (Pythia 0.345) is a capability measure, not representational alignment. It does not bear on V7's claims about incompleteness, plateau, or causes of alignment. Re-linked to none; recorded under fits_no_version.

rows.check: The partial correlation (+0.30, p=0.009) controlling for scale concerns alignment vs. capability gap, not convergence itself. Re-linked to none.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Experiment A’s matched-scale retrieval comparison and 74 cross-family pairs
reader_labels.reason: Despite rising alignment, retrieval capability stratifies by architecture, and alignment correlates positively with the absolute capability gap (A2–A6). This qualifies any inference from representational convergence to capability convergence; the study does not establish a plateau or identify shared data/objectives as the cause.
